posts.title: Nanjing in Three Days and Three Nights — the Republican Era and Hongshan Forest Zoo
posts.description: Two forms of great love, reached by different roads yet arriving at the same place. Photo Album: View the album for this trip Travel Guide: Get the itinerary By the standards of tourist cities, Nanjing’s content is extraordinarily rich. Before we left I asked my wife: Nanjing can be played many ways — the Six Dynasties (mostly before the Sui and Tang), the Ming, the Republican era, the War of Resistance, the zoo, the Yangtze, natural scenery, and a great many museums. What do you want to see? She said the Republican era. Then, thinking of our daughter, we added the top-tier Hongshan Forest Zoo and cut museums down to a minimum. The goal was clear; the trip happened; we set off. Day 1: Hongshan Forest Zoo I first learned of this zoo from Hua Shi’s book Visiting Zoos Is Serious Business, which systematically lays out the character, the pros and cons, and the essential mission of zoos around the world. posts.title: A Toy Port for My Daughter
posts.description: A small experiment in tidying education and task management. Last night my daughter broke a large toy beetle, and its wings and head came off. I meant to fix it myself, but then it occurred to me that she could watch how I approach a problem. I picked up the beetle body and the wing and said, this wing came off, but I did not pay attention to how it was before, so I do not know how to put it back. What should I do? Hey, its two wings are the same, so let me look at how the other wing is attached. Hearing this, my daughter understood right away, said she would fix it, and took the toy beetle to study. But it has a rather delicate spring mechanism: the two ends of a wire must be inserted into two holes before the insect wings will flap and spring back with the wind-up. I guessed she would not notice or understand this, but I still let her try first. posts.title: How AI Taught My Daughter to Take a Bath
posts.description: Everyone asks what AI can do at work, but few ask what it can do in daily life. My daughter recently learned to take a bath. But it is more that she is no longer afraid of water. She still cannot get the order right and misses some spots. She also dawdles terribly, and starts playing the moment she is in the water. I scolded her, but then thought it was doing little good, so I decided to turn bath time into a game instead. I had AI generate an image like this and printed two copies to bring home. One is simply a coloring page for my daughter to play with. On the other, she cuts out the pieces one by one. She knows some numbers now, so she lines them up in order, and together we tape them to the outside of the shower glass. This way she has a checklist to clear level by level while bathing, and I hope she remembers the steps while dawdling less. After using it for a week, the effect was immediate.
